name: Rye Crisp
beta: Dramatic laybacking along a flake that opens leftward, followed by more flakes and some jamming, ends at a bolted anchor. A direct start via the neighbouring crack is possible. Gear to a #4 cam.
overview: Stunning laybacking up a flake facing left, followed by more flakes and some jamming. A direct start via the crack on its left is possible.

current.area_walk_in: Essentially no approach: a short trail from the parking area leads straight to the base.
current.descent: rap using two ropes

name: Sabbatical
beta: Begin on the wall beside Humble's Tumble (on its right), work across the overlaps, then two bolts lead up and rightward; medium cams assist.
overview: Climbs across the overlaps, then two bolts lead rightward and up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Rightward from Humble's Tumble, on the face

name: Siesta
beta: Begin in Crack of Dung, step out rightward to bolt one; four additional clips then take you along the arete.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Sinsemilla
beta: Begin like Just Say No, veer right after roughly twenty feet, then continue directly upward by a pair of old bolts and across an overlap.
overview: Begins like Just Say No, veers right after roughly 20 ft, then goes straight up past a pair of ancient bolts, then an overlap.

current.area_walk_in: Essentially no approach: a short trail from the parking area leads straight to the base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Begins as Just Say No does

name: Strawberry Jam
beta: Face climbing leads by a bolt (the crux) into a broad crack and easier ground; if the crux defeats you, sidestep right from that bolt, surmount the little roof, and angle back left into the crack.
overview: Face climbing past a bolt (the crux) to a wide crack with easier climbing above. If it shuts you down, step right off the bolt, go over a mini roof, and return to the crack leftward.

current.descent: rap from the Pygmies anchor

name: Stress Fracture
beta: A corner crack opening rightward leads past a roof to the summit, optionally broken in half; the crux sits low in the corner partway up to the roof, and large cams protect the roof.
overview: Climbs a corner crack that faces right, getting past a roof; it may be split into two pitches. The hardest moves are in the corner about halfway up to the roof. Large cams are wanted for the roof.

current.area_walk_in: Follow clear paths around either the left or right end of the rock to reach its back side.
current.descent: double-rope rappel down the west face, or walk south for two single-rope raps

name: Swiss Cheese
beta: A steep wall full of holes. The opening is easy ground up to bolt one, and the upper part takes medium cams in the neighbouring crack on the left.
overview: A sheer wall that resembles a block of holey cheese. It begins on easy ground with a long gap before the first bolt, and mid-size cams in the left-hand crack can supplement the top section.

current.descent: single-rope rappel

name: Tarantula
beta: Steep, thin climbing with a sting; beyond the roof, keep to the left of the bolts.
overview: Thin and steep with a stinging crux. Above the roof the line stays left of the bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Circle Bath Rock on its right-hand side to reach the centre of the western wall; the Rollercoaster Wall lies behind the rock.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Roughly 20 ft rightward from Wild Country's crack

name: Testosterone Test
beta: A direct line straight up the middle of the face; little TCUs and supplementary cams are essential.
overview: A direct line through the face's centre that needs small TCUs and extra cams.

current.area_walk_in: A hundred-yard stroll to the big west-facing wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Directly up the centre of the face

name: The Pygmies Got Stoned
beta: A rounded arete dividing the north face from the east, offering eight bolts of continuous friction and face moves.
overview: Follows the rounded arete separating the north face from the east face, with sustained friction plus face moves.

current.area_walk_in: Essentially no approach: a short trail from the parking area leads straight to the base.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Thin Slice
beta: Follow the sharp finger-width crack through huecos and multi-coloured rock; solid face holds and excellent protection arrive precisely when needed. Little cams, wires and slings are enough.
overview: A steep finger crack climbs through huecos and colourful rock, with good holds on the face and reliable gear exactly when needed. It ends at a bolted anchor.

current.descent: double-rope rappel, or a single 60 m rope

name: Tow Away Zone
beta: A tough start in a thin crack, then past a roof with a bolt, then the superb hand crack above; an easy traverse rightward reaches the Pretty Face anchor, and the opening can be backed up with small cams.
overview: A thin crack opens the route with hard moves, then a roof protected by a bolt leads to a superb hand-sized crack. A simple rightward traverse ends at the neighbouring route's anchor.

current.area_walk_in: Follow clear paths around either the left or right end of the rock to reach its back side.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: shared with the Pretty Face route

name: Triple Roofs
beta: Head for the big three-cornered roof, skirt it on its left, step back into the crack on the right and follow that to the top; another finish traverses leftward to the anchors above Something Sporting.
overview: Goes to the big triangular roof, passes on its left side and returns rightward into the crack, which runs to the top. Alternatively, finish by moving across to Something Sporting's anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Wheat Thin
beta: A lovely thin crack that curves up the wall, reached via a scramble over the face just beside the tree on its right; take a full rack.
overview: A gorgeous thin crack arcing up the wall; get started by scrambling the lower face on the tree's right side.

current.area_walk_in: Essentially no approach: a short trail from the parking area leads straight to the base.
current.descent: rap Rye Crisp using two ropes

name: Blue Roof
beta:
First pitch: start with gear placed off someone's shoulders or from a stick, aid until it goes free, then trace the crack leftward and up to the fixed belay.

Second pitch: traverse rightward under the big roof until you balance on an iron flake the size of a plate, then crank the obvious roof-capped dihedral crack; carry varied natural protection, including TCUs.
overview: Pitch one is aided or freed up a finger-to-hand crack to a fixed belay. The second pitch traverses rightward under a large roof to a flake the size of a dinner plate, then cranks a dihedral and roof crack.

current.descent: rappel from the anchor far out to the right on a shelf

name: Devil's Lake Dreams
beta: Follow the splitter hand-to-fist crack to its bulging exit moves, then finish by the large cedar tree; varied natural gear.
overview: A splitting crack that finishes with bulging moves, topping out at a large cedar.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: a splitter hand crack just right of Kaya

name: Settled Controversy
beta: Layback the large flake to the horn on top and then trend rightward to finish; protection is a small nut and a mid-size cam.
overview: A route up a big layback flake topped by a horn, starting behind a boulder as big as a car, exiting rightward.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: hidden behind a boulder the size of a car, 40 ft along from Wizard's Hat toward the left

name: Suspended Animation
beta: Follow the line with a central crack; it drifts right near the top, and finishing straight up is the harder variation. Mixed protection: two quickdraws and a mid-size piece.
overview: A crack splits the centre of the wall and the route drifts rightward near the finish; going straight out instead makes it harder.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: The Bolted One
beta: Follow the clear-cut dihedral crack at the hallway's main corner; protection is mixed (varied sizes plus a bolt), and wires work nicely high up.
overview: The conspicuous dihedral crack that makes up the hallway's chief corner. The upper half takes wired nuts nicely, and the lone bolt gave the route its name.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the clear-cut dihedral crack forming the hallway's chief corner

name: The Dagger
beta: Shuffle rightward along the roof edge to the arete, then ascend directly to the ledge using small natural gear.
overview: A short route that begins with a foot traverse across the edge of a knee-high roof, reaching the arete.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: The Off-Width Exam
beta: Inhale to stick, exhale and gain an inch, and repeat; it has seen a number of lead ascents since, one using wooden blocks for protection.
overview: A big offwidth that begins in an overhanging, symmetrical dihedral, a three-star classic that demands patience.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: a big offwidth rising from the base of an overhanging dihedral with symmetrical walls

name: Techno Destructo
beta: Start by the tree, just beyond So Low, and climb in much the same vertical edging style as that neighbor.
overview: A vertical edging problem that sees little traffic, and climbs in much the same manner as its neighbour So Low.

current.area_walk_in: From the parking lot, follow the trail system toward the Motherlode and take the left-hand fork.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Starts beside a big tree just beyond So Low

name: Pushing Up Daisies
beta: Leave the old chains with a hard pull off a sloping ledge onto easier ground, then pull a committing deadpoint from two crimps to the top-out jug. Two extra bolts go in beyond Flour Power.
overview: Adds a couple of bolts above Flour Power so that the climb ends at the rim. Leaving the old chains takes one tough step from a rounded shelf, followed by an exposed lunge from a pair of crimps to the final jug.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Extends Flour Power beyond its original lower-off to the cliff rim

name: 8 Ball
beta: Start by a small rhododendron and get through a blank-looking low section, then angle up and left to the prominent right-facing corner. Follow that dihedral to its end and continue over the pocketed wall and on to the chains.
overview: An unpromising smooth bottom section gives way as the line veers up-left into a prominent corner. That dihedral is climbed to where it ends, and a pocketed face then leads to the chains.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Beside a small rhododendron bush, on its right

name: A Confederacy of Dunces
beta: Opening bolts one through three sit on dirty, fragile rock; once past them, everything above improves somewhat.
overview: The opening three bolts pass loose, dirty stone; the climbing improves modestly above that.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the Animal Crackers trail and keep going several hundred feet past that wall to a steep ravine beside a large amphitheater. Descend the sandy ravine, step across a little creek at the bottom, then go a short way up and around a corner to the overhanging main wall. The routes at the far end lie about 100 feet beyond it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Rightmost line of a separate section of wall, down a ravine about 50 yards left of the main wall

name: A Way of Life
beta: Start at the right side and work leftward, passing a vintage piton plus three bolts that spin, to reach the top. Descend by walking off to the right.
overview: A line on the detached pinnacle near where the approach trail meets the cliff, protected by a few bolts and an old piton. It heads leftward as it climbs and finishes on top.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the stream and go roughly 150 ft farther, then take the trail that forks right ahead of a large boulder. It crosses a short muddy flat and climbs uphill to meet the cliff at Coffee Talk, by the base of an isolated pinnacle.
current.descent: walk off right
current.location: bolts running behind a big tree, 35 ft to the right of Coffee Talk

name: Acrophobiacs Anonymous
beta: Trend up and to the left across the slab toward the shared anchors.
overview: Perhaps the Red's easiest bolted route: a brief slab just right of the neighboring crack climb, angling up to anchors shared with a neighbor.

current.area_walk_in: Where the path arrives at the cliff below Slabalito, keep going leftward and a bit uphill, passing under a low overhang for roughly 150 feet, until a cluster of short bolted climbs and the conspicuous chimney of the Dragon routes appear.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Ale-8-One
beta:
Go up the flake until the first bolt is clipped, move rightward and make one hard pull onto a jug. Shake out there and drift back slightly left.

Above, big moves on the overhanging face lead to a difficult finish using edges and gastons.
overview: Sustained overhanging face climbing with big moves and a tough finish involving edges and gastons, beginning with a flake.

current.area_walk_in: Walk toward the right from Madness Cave to reach a lower, less steep wall holding many lines. The first line met is The Sauce, beside a large tree that grows against the cliff.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: All in a Day's Work
beta: Follow the wide crack set in a shallow, narrow dihedral, stemming and grinding upward; large cams suit the crack.
overview: A broad crack set in a shallow, narrow-angled corner; stem, grunt and slither to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Go straight back from the clearing about 100 feet until an old logging track branches up the hillside leftward. Follow it 150 feet, then turn up the slope to the right along a barely visible path angling right up to a ridge. Turn right on top and follow the ridge trail for roughly five minutes until a small pinnacle shows at the cliff's end. Go left around the pinnacle to the main wall for the left-side routes, or loop around toward the wall's right-hand portion for the others.
current.descent: tree rappel

name: Anne's Crack
beta:
The start is mossy, but the crack gets better quickly as you go up.

Large cams are handy for building the belay at the ledge.
overview: A hand crack, mossy at the bottom but cleaner higher, reaching a ledge.

current.area_walk_in: A flat, well-made trail winds through pleasant surroundings; this is among the longer walks in the area. The cliff is reached by that path, and a line of bolts runs up the main arete to your left as you arrive.
current.descent: abseil off a tree
current.location: hand crack about 50 ft past Gorge Factor 10

name: Another One Fights the Rust
beta: The crux comes low and has bolt protection, and you top out onto the ledge above.
overview: A gently overhanging dihedral that faces right, with the crux low down and ending on a ledge.

current.area_walk_in: Where the path arrives at the cliff below Slabalito, keep going leftward and a bit uphill, passing under a low overhang for roughly 150 feet, until a cluster of short bolted climbs and the conspicuous chimney of the Dragon routes appear.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 50 ft to the right of Crescendo

name: Apoplectic Chick from Missouri
beta: Pass through the overhanging lower part to reach a blank face; work out that section, after which larger holds lead the rest of the way to the anchors.
overview: Begins on a steep, overhanging stretch, meets a blank stretch of face, then eases onto bigger holds for the run to the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: around the corner and to the right of the previous line

name: Aquaduck Pocket
beta: Start from the ramp that a big boulder forms, pick the correct pockets through the steep part, then cruise up bigger holds until you reach the anchors.
overview: Pick the right pockets through the steep lower section, then cruise on bigger edges to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: First of three bolt lines on a steep wall; starts up a ramp made by a big boulder

name: Avalanche Run
beta: Positive holds lead to the intimidating roof, which is marked by a fixed draw. Locate the crucial holds, cut your feet loose, and fight the barn-door swing, then hold on until the chains.
overview: A big, conspicuous roof defines it. Solid holds bring you under the roof, where you must find the critical holds, let the feet swing free and hope you stay on, and keep gripping until the chains.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: marked by a prominent big roof carrying a fixed draw

name: Back Door to Paris
beta: Locate the pedestal, then follow the face on its left, clipping bolts up to anchors beneath the bulge.
overview: A bolted face climb that starts beside a pedestal of rock and ends beneath a pronounced bulge.

current.area_walk_in: A steep trail leads uphill from the pulloff to the cliff. It is distinct at the start but easy to lose, so follow it carefully to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: just right of Are the Pies Fresh?, up the face left of a rock pedestal

name: Bandolier
beta: The face leans out a bit and has a pair of cruxes; a hands-free rest lies off to the left if wanted. A steep flake near the top gets very pumpy before the chains.
overview: An ideal first taste of pump-inducing gorge sandstone for visiting 5.11 climbers. Two cruxes are followed by an optional hands-free rest off to the left; the last steep flake is where the forearms give out, just under the chains.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Wall immediately beyond Wadcutter, going left

name: Bedtime for Bonzo
beta:
Pitch one: go up the ramp to a big ledge and belay from bolts.

Pitch two: go right via a hallway toward the next start, climb the dihedral that faces right until a hand-sized ledge, shuffle along that ledge into a fist crack angling right, and follow it to the top.
overview: A two-pitch outing. The first pitch follows a ramp up to a big ledge with a bolted belay. After a short walk right through a gap in the rock, pitch two climbs a dihedral facing right to a hand ledge, crosses it, and finishes up a fist crack that angles right. A summit view tops it off.

current.descent: rappel from the bolted anchors
current.location: Beyond The Turret at the wall's far left, where an obvious dihedral faces left behind a little tree

name: Beene Material
beta: A tight corner with a few overhanging steps along the way, ending at a tree anchor.
overview: Meander through overhangs in a narrow corner to reach a tree anchor.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the wooden footbridge and keep straight; a branch heads right about 20 feet beyond it. Follow that path uphill roughly ten minutes to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Next to a massive overhang, tucked beneath a big rhododendron, a narrow corner

name: Blue Runner
beta:
Head for the roof roughly twenty feet off the ground, then shift leftward and upward into the dihedral.

Stem the dihedral through an obvious thin crux into a wide crack, which goes on to the ledge; two very large cams help with that wide part.
overview: Starts up to a small overhang, drifts left to gain a dihedral, and stems up it through an unmistakably thin spot into a wide crack that ends at the ledge.

current.descent: rappel from bolted anchors

name: Beeper
beta: Start from the big boulders at the base, latch the arete and ride it until it becomes a narrow crack, which carries on to the anchors.
overview: Pull onto the rib and trace it over crumbly stone into a slender fissure, which leads to the anchors. The rock becomes poor near the top.

current.area_walk_in: Go back to the road, cross it, and follow the gravel track uphill for about 0.2 miles, then take the trail that cuts left up to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 20 ft right of Dogleg, on a rib that carries a lofty corner, starting from large blocks at its foot
